compiler scaffolding (Supplies evidence for the #gaps verify of the gap review; the source asks for the gap check but names no command.): SKILL.md:137: exec gaps check from checks as gapcheck

over_asking: R3: when the request is unclear about building, the flow asks the user to choose between planning and implementation and requires confirmation (lines 53-57), but the source makes planning the default for that case

questions: Does the 'Ground the scope' paragraph (SKILL.md line 14) require actually inspecting code in every run, or only when a repository exists?
Is the work registry required to be created when none exists (SKILL.md 44) outside standalone use, where creation is only 'when implementation work needs tracking'?
What counts as 'costly-to-reverse' and 'consequential' (SKILL.md 18) — left to agent judgment?

R3 and R66 carry evidence `user`, but the source says a build request authorizes implementation and forbids repeated approval. I did not add an ask for them. The mode is a branch on whether the request asks to build or implement. Should an explicit confirmation be added anyway?

The two decision asks (settle the missing outcome or authority decision; approve deployment, publication, tool installation, or delegation) have no `user-decides` entries. The inline layout has no authority header, so I couldn't add them. Does your checker need them?

I wrote the exec IDs as `exec #status ...` with the ID right after `exec`, following the `write #id` / `verify #id` pattern. The guide only shows the `exec#id` form in order rules. Please confirm this parses.
Does the checker accept `exec readonly <text> from checks as <name>` without an ID before the first dismissible ask (M1)? I used it so the inspection exec can precede the R11 ask.
assumptions: Table rows in terminology.md are grouped as context requirements (definitions that guide decisions), not individual requirements.

SKILL.md line 40 is a heading ('Deliver and verify' is actually line 40; line 38 contains the gap-check text). Some line spans for R23/R24 and heading attribution may be off by one: R23/R24 content is on line 38, and line 40 is the heading.
Evidence 'self' used where the agent's own judgment suffices; 'exec' where checks or inspection are run.
Corrected SKILL.md line spans for the numbered design activities and Bound/Check paragraphs (R16-R24) to match the listing; the previous inventory had them shifted, leaving lines 27 and 29 uncovered.
Fixed the R89 span to start at line 23, since lines 21-22 are the table header.

The references are consulted through the `apply` step meanings (terminology, existing-projects, design-method, research, artifacts, implementation), not through `read` statements. A `read` into a conditional binding would be unbound on the other path.

Recording a gap and continuing is the repair for every soft failure (missing reference, declined permission, failed fit check, failed validation). The only `retry` is the implementation repair loop. That loop exits through a blocker return when the same failure repeats or a required capability is missing.
The R50 `L150` anchor for `retry` assumes my line count of the delivered file. The `retry` line is at 150.
R88-R92 (context, evidence none) are kept as short vocabulary bullets in the Context section.
Inspection of the subject is a `read` into `evidence`, not an `exec`. That keeps all execs after the asks, so nothing mutates before a dismissible ask (M1).
R3/R66 user evidence is landed as a conditional ask that fires only when the request does not say whether to plan or build, which keeps 'no repeated approval' for requests that already state it.
Declining the plan-or-build ask defaults the run to planning (design-only) instead of aborting.
Contract sections are ordered always, never, inputs, order, to fix F2.
The `evidence` binding is replaced by `inspection`, the result of the readonly exec. That fixes U1, because the exec binds it on every path.
A shared `gaps` binding is started at the top, extended at each recorded gap, and returned on every path, so gaps stay visible instead of aborting.
Line anchors L54, L60, L75 and L176 refer to the three `require confirmation` lines and the single `retry` in SKILL.md as written, counting from line 1 (the opening `---`).

Planning is the default, so the plan-versus-build ask was replaced by a branch on whether the request asks to build or implement; no user prompt is needed because the source says a build request authorizes implementation.

The technology-fit check now runs after alternatives are compared and before the research step that selects or recommends one. A failed check records a gap, and the research step and a never-rule bar recommending adoption of an unchecked candidate.
Line references L60, L75 and L176 were counted by hand against the new SKILL.md: L60 and L75 are the require confirmation lines, and L176 is the retry line.
R3/R66 user evidence is landed as an ask that fires only when the request does not say whether to build or implement; a clear build request needs no approval, and a decline defaults to planning.
The roadmap-row check (R60) stays a conditional branch, now anchored to R60.
The gap-review exec is reported as scaffolding; the remaining W9, W5 and W15 warnings are intentional because the source says to record gaps and continue.
